newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Japan buys January jet fuel at $1.55/bbl premium.
newsitem.headline: Japan buys January jet fuel at $1.55/bbl premium.

text.p: Japan bought its first jet fuel cargoes for January 1997 arrival at about $1.55 over Singapore spot quotes on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis, almost unchanged from the premiums it paid for December barrels, industry sources said on Tuesday.
"The premiums for January are quite low. It reflects the ample supplies in the area," one trader at a Japanese trading house said.
A Japanese refiner bought two 30,000-tonne cargoes for arrival in January at between $1.50 and $1.55 per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f basis, traders said.
Players were surprised at the relatively low premium paid for Janaury cargoes as tradtionally premiums would pick up substaintially during the peak winter period.
Last year, Japanese endusers paid more than $3.00 premiums for cargoes delivered in January.
Singapore swap quotes for the jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) firmed slightly on Tuesday on renewed buying from North Asia, traders said.
December regrade picked up slightly with bids seen late afternoon at 40 cents from Friday's 10/35 cents.
"The market was boosted by talks that North Asia was back for its winter requirement," one trader said.
But many feel that the pickup is likely to be short lived as there are ample stocks throughout the region's independent storage terminals.
So far Japan has already bought three cargoes for arrival in December at around the $1.50 a barrel premium mark. It bought a total of four cargoes for arrival in November, traders said.
